claude.sample_unit: clinical notes per task (agitation and malnutrition tasks, each n = 208)

links.outcome: Whether retrieval strategies in RAG improve grounding, answer quality and item-level accuracy for clinical information extraction
links.effect: Reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperformed standalone BM25 and dense retrieval; dense reranking gave Answer F1 0.946 and Item-level Accuracy 0.963 for agitation; ensemble methods gave 0.944 for malnutrition.
links.quote: A repeated-measures ANOVA reveals that reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperform both standalone sparse (BM25) and dense retrieval across both tasks.

unlisted_practices: Comparison of retrieval strategies (sparse, dense, reranking, fusion) within RAG pipelines for clinical information extraction

openai.sample_unit: clinical named-entity extraction cases; 208 per task
models_evaluated: dense retrieval with cross-encoder rerank RAG
dynamic linear fusion of sparse and dense scores RAG

links.outcome: same-data comparison of RAG retrieval methods
links.effect: Reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperformed BM25 and dense; agitation Answer F1 0.946, item accuracy 0.963; malnutrition best item accuracy 0.944.
links.quote: A repeated-measures ANOVA reveals that reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperform both standalone sparse (BM25) and dense retrieval across both tasks.

links.effect: Three error types were identified: intrinsic hallucination, extrinsic hallucination, and false negatives.
links.quote: Through error analysis, we identify three LLM error types in clinical named entity recognition: intrinsic hallucination, extrinsic hallucination, and false negatives, and elucidate how RAG mitigates each.

unlisted_practices: Using reranking-based or hybrid ensemble retrieval instead of standalone sparse or dense retrieval in clinical RAG information extraction.
